svg.aria-label: How to write quia: 4 letters, q, u, i, a, one after another
svg.title: Writing quia
svg.desc: 4 letters written one after another: q, u, i, a (latin). Each letter has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that letter, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/LatinPrint-Subset.ttf. Each letter is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the letters are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: q: Grundschrift-App (Laborschule Bielefeld, Bielefeld University, with the Grundschulverband), level kleinbuchstaben/q, ordered stroke paths for q (assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/q/metadata.json, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only) <https://github.com/Medien-Treibhaus/grundschrift-app-source/blob/f6dbd807adbb3fc2f94207fe578def439f6e9c49/assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/q/metadata.json>; u: Grundschrift-App (Laborschule Bielefeld, Bielefeld University, with the Grundschulverband), level kleinbuchstaben/u, ordered stroke paths for u (assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/u/metadata.json, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only) <https://github.com/Medien-Treibhaus/grundschrift-app-source/blob/f6dbd807adbb3fc2f94207fe578def439f6e9c49/assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/u/metadata.json>; i: Grundschrift-App (Laborschule Bielefeld, Bielefeld University, with the Grundschulverband), level kleinbuchstaben/i, ordered stroke paths for i (assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/i/metadata.json, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only) <https://github.com/Medien-Treibhaus/grundschrift-app-source/blob/f6dbd807adbb3fc2f94207fe578def439f6e9c49/assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/i/metadata.json>; a: Grundschrift-App (Laborschule Bielefeld, Bielefeld University, with the Grundschulverband), level kleinbuchstaben/a, ordered stroke paths for a (assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/a/metadata.json, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only) <https://github.com/Medien-Treibhaus/grundschrift-app-source/blob/f6dbd807adbb3fc2f94207fe578def439f6e9c49/assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/a/metadata.json>. Source notes on variation: q: The Grundschrift-App was made in a research project of the Laborschule at Bielefeld University with the Grundschulverband, on its Grundschrift school model, with a teacher advisory team. Each letter is an ordered list of paths, one per pen-down stroke, which the app makes a child trace in order. It writes q in one stroke: anticlockwise round the bowl from the top right, back up to the top of the stem, and down the stem below the line. UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of q, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. Only 26 of the 120 are one stroke, the source's count; all 26 start at the top and go anticlockwise round the bowl. 89 are two strokes, and in 83 of those 89 the second stroke is a short level line across the foot of the stem, a habit of these writers' hand that the printed q does not have. The app's repository has no licence, so only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are taken from it; no point is copied, and the path is fitted to the q of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer. u: The Grundschrift-App was made in a research project of the Laborschule at Bielefeld University with the Grundschulverband, on its Grundschrift school model, with a teacher advisory team. Each letter is an ordered list of paths, one per pen-down stroke, which the app makes a child trace in order. It writes u in one stroke: down from the top left, round the bottom and up, then down the right side. Grundschrift ends the stroke with a small hook to the right that the bundled outline does not print, so the path ends where the printed letter ends. UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of u, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. All 120 are one stroke, and 85 start at the top left. The app's repository has no licence, so only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are taken from it; no point is copied, and the path is fitted to the u of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer. i: The Grundschrift-App was made in a research project of the Laborschule at Bielefeld University with the Grundschulverband, on its Grundschrift school model, with a teacher advisory team. Each letter is an ordered list of paths, one per pen-down stroke, which the app makes a child trace in order. It writes i in two strokes: the stem first, from the top down, and the dot last. Grundschrift ends the stroke with a small hook to the right that the bundled outline does not print, so the path ends where the printed letter ends. UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of i, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. 115 of the 120 are two strokes, and in all 115 the dot, the shorter stroke, comes last. The app's repository has no licence, so only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are taken from it; no point is copied, and the path is fitted to the i of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer. a: The Grundschrift-App was made in a research project of the Laborschule at Bielefeld University with the Grundschulverband, on its Grundschrift school model, with a teacher advisory team. Each letter is an ordered list of paths, one per pen-down stroke, which the app makes a child trace in order. It writes the one-storey a in one stroke: anticlockwise round the bowl from the top right, back up to the top of the stem, and down the stem to the foot. The printed a joins the bowl to the stem, so the path runs back up the stem to its top before it comes down, as the source does. UJIpenchars2 (Prat, Castro, Llorens, Marzal and Vilar; UCI Machine Learning Repository dataset 177, CC BY 4.0) holds 120 tablet pen traces of a, two by each of 60 adult Spanish writers; only counts are cited. 118 of the 120 are one stroke, the source's count; 92 of those 118 start at the top (72 top centre, 20 top right), and 111 go anticlockwise round the bowl. The app's repository has no licence, so only the order, the start, the direction and the lifts are taken from it; no point is copied, and the path is fitted to the a of the bundled LatinPrint-Subset.ttf, a renamed subset of SIL Global's literacy typeface Andika 7.000, which prints the one-storey a the school model teaches; the book's own text face is a different font. Handwriting varies by writer.
svg.text: How it is written — 4 letters, one after another
Letter 1 of 4 — one unbroken stroke · 2 movements
Letter 2 of 4 — one unbroken stroke · 2 movements
Letter 4 of 4 — one unbroken stroke · 2 movements
Letter 1: stroke order after Grundschrift-App (Laborschule Bielefeld, Bielefeld University, with the Grundschulverband), level kleinbuchstaben/q, ordered stroke paths for q
(assets/levels/kleinbuchstaben/q/metadata.json, commit f6dbd80; no licence, facts only)

Letter 4: stroke order after Grundschrift-App (Laborschule Bielefeld, Bielefeld University, with the Grundschulverband), level kleinbuchstaben/a, ordered stroke paths for a
